selection_rule: A twenty-two-unit thesis-to-method route through the canonical manifest. Each unit has one representative canonical chapter and may synthesize adjacent reference owners without forking their claims. The route covers the stack thesis; efficiency; authority and failure; evidence; constitutional and objective governance; capability replacement; intent; planning; world models; compilation; context; memory; verification; claim review; work and artifacts; effects and operations; replaceable substrates; developmental learning; readiness and liveness; resource and recovery economics; recursive integration; and the living research program. All 84 chapters remain canonical architecture-reference owners.

chapters.reader_question: Why should advanced AI be treated as governed responsibilities and transitions rather than one opaque model?
chapters.running_example: Start one repository change by separating capability, authority, context, plan, effect, observation, evidence, and replacement.
chapters.strongest_objection: A sufficiently capable end-to-end model may preserve more information with less bureaucracy than an explicit stack.
chapters.failure_story: The change succeeds, but nobody can reconstruct who authorized it, what changed, or how to recover it.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Matched natural deployments showing simpler monolithic operation is equally controllable, observable, recoverable, useful, and affordable would narrow the thesis.
chapters.handoff: The efficiency unit asks whether explicit routing and reuse can earn their governance and lifecycle costs.

chapters.reader_question: Can governed routing, reuse, and specialist computation improve useful capability without hiding displaced costs?
chapters.running_example: Compare frontier-model-only work with a routed repository change that reuses context, specialists, tests, and independent checks.
chapters.strongest_objection: The accounting and verification required by a stack may cost more than using the strongest model throughout.
chapters.failure_story: A cheap route looks efficient only because repair, reviewer burden, false refusal, and residual effects were excluded.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Matched workloads with full lifecycle accounting and no risk-adjusted cost or quality advantage would reject or narrow the hypothesis.
chapters.handoff: Efficiency is meaningful only after the next unit defines authority ceilings and ordinary failure boundaries.

chapters.reader_question: Which boundaries separate proposal, approval, execution, observation, and release, and how do failures remain owned?
chapters.running_example: Let the planner draft a patch while a current scoped grant alone permits a bounded adapter to alter the tree.
chapters.strongest_objection: Typed boundaries can become ceremonial metadata when the runtime can ignore, forge, or bypass them.
chapters.failure_story: A low-authority planner borrows a broad stale credential and the resulting failure is assigned to no detector or owner.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Simpler permission systems resisting revocation, confused-deputy, bypass, and residual-loss attacks equally well would justify a smaller boundary model.
chapters.handoff: The evidence unit now asks how records about those boundaries can change belief without inheriting support.

chapters.reader_question: How can claims change while capability, authority, context, receipts, proofs, and publication remain noninheriting states?
chapters.running_example: Let one repository test strengthen a narrow result without promoting the architecture claim or turning a receipt into reality.
chapters.strongest_objection: Support labels may create an aura of rigor while the underlying evidence remains narrow, stale, dependent, or weak.
chapters.failure_story: A schema receipt becomes a runtime-safety claim through repeated prose even though no independent effect was observed.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Natural correction streams showing no improvement over a simpler review protocol would force a smaller claim-transition system.
chapters.handoff: Claim discipline next meets constitutions, values, objectives, and the problem of legitimate protected change.

chapters.reader_question: How should constitutions, conflicting values, learned objectives, human factors, and legitimate amendment interact?
chapters.running_example: A repository request conflicts with a protected policy and a user preference, forcing contestable interpretation rather than silent optimization.
chapters.strongest_objection: A formal constitution can freeze contested values, centralize power, and offer only the appearance of alignment.
chapters.failure_story: The system satisfies a literal rule while manipulating the user, hiding the conflict, and controlling the amendment evidence.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Pluralistic governance mechanisms with fewer capture, rigidity, and burden failures would replace or sharply narrow the constitutional substrate.
chapters.handoff: The next unit turns protected capabilities into replaceable fields whose qualification cannot be inherited.

chapters.reader_question: How can a capability retain a stable contract while its model, memory, router, tool, or substrate changes?
chapters.running_example: Replace the patch verifier while preserving the exact capability contract, regression envelope, authority ceiling, and recovery route.
chapters.strongest_objection: A stable field may hide semantic drift and make incomparable components look interchangeable.
chapters.failure_story: A faster replacement inherits its predecessor's name and readiness but silently drops the attack that justified the field.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Natural replacement studies showing no continuity or recovery benefit over conventional versioning would weaken the field abstraction.
chapters.handoff: Stable capabilities become useful when a human request is compiled into an exact command without inventing authority.

chapters.reader_question: How does an ambiguous human request become bounded work without inventing authority, success criteria, or certainty?
chapters.running_example: Translate a repository chapter-improvement request into target files, allowed operations, evidence duties, stop rules, and approval conditions.
chapters.strongest_objection: A precise command contract can harden a mistaken interpretation and make ambiguity harder to notice.
chapters.failure_story: The system completes the literal patch while violating the user's actual constraint because uncertainty became an unstated default.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: User studies showing lighter clarification produces fewer intent failures at lower burden would justify a smaller contract.
chapters.handoff: The planning unit turns the accepted command into dependencies and alternatives without turning the plan into permission.

chapters.reader_question: How can a plan coordinate dependencies and replanning while remaining a proposal rather than implicit execution authority?
chapters.running_example: Represent the repository change as source inspection, drafting, verification, tests, rollback preparation, and release or refusal.
chapters.strongest_objection: Detailed plans are expensive and brittle when the environment changes faster than the plan can be checked.
chapters.failure_story: A stale plan executes after its context, dependency, and authorization assumptions have changed.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Dynamic-task studies showing direct reactive control is safer and more efficient would narrow when explicit planning should activate.
chapters.handoff: Planning requires a world model that keeps predictions, branches, interventions, and actual observations separate.

chapters.reader_question: How should a system predict, simulate, intervene, and reconcile without confusing possible worlds with actual state?
chapters.running_example: Predict the patch's effects in a branch, run a bounded intervention, and reconcile the prediction with the observed tree.
chapters.strongest_objection: World-model governance may add records without improving prediction, causal identification, or grounding.
chapters.failure_story: A simulated passing state overwrites actual repository state and later planning treats the branch as observed fact.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Strong predictive and causal baselines with simpler branch discipline and equal calibration would justify collapsing the extra machinery.
chapters.handoff: The compilation unit converts qualified meaning into executable representations while preserving declared semantic loss.

chapters.reader_question: How can intent, beliefs, relations, and constraints be lowered into executable forms without silently changing meaning?
chapters.running_example: Lower the repository-change contract into planner predicates, verifier queries, tool calls, and recovery obligations with traceable losses.
chapters.strongest_objection: Semantic intermediate representations may be brittle private languages that lose nuance while pretending to preserve it.
chapters.failure_story: A compiler preserves field names but drops the constraint that the verifier must be independent of the proposer.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: End-to-end systems preserving intent and observability better without an explicit semantic IR would narrow the compiler boundary.
chapters.handoff: The context unit packages the exact sources, branches, taint, tools, and omissions consumed by compiled work.

chapters.reader_question: What interface lets models consume paged, cached, mounted, and tainted context without treating it as belief or authority?
chapters.running_example: Mount repository source files, policy history, summaries, and cached work as versioned context pages with explicit omissions and rights.
chapters.strongest_objection: A typed context ABI may add latency and false precision while retrieval errors still determine the answer.
chapters.failure_story: A stale cached summary is mounted under a current name and silently authorizes removal of a deliberate safety check.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Simpler retrieval and caching systems matching adequacy, provenance, revocation, and cost would justify a thinner ABI.
chapters.handoff: The memory unit decides what may persist as revisable belief or reusable procedure after the task.

chapters.reader_question: How do qualified observations become durable beliefs and successful traces become revisable procedures rather than frozen mistakes?
chapters.running_example: Store the patch rationale as a defeasible belief and compile the validated workflow into a skill with regressions and retirement.
chapters.strongest_objection: Structured memory and procedural consolidation can amplify early errors and create opaque path dependence.
chapters.failure_story: One successful trace becomes a default skill, then survives after its policy, dependency, and safety assumptions expire.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Continual-learning baselines with less structure and equal revision, forgetting, transfer, and recovery would narrow the design.
chapters.handoff: The verification unit asks whether the available context and reviewer capacity can actually test the resulting claims.

chapters.reader_question: When does relevant context still fail to provide enough independent comparison capacity for a risky judgment?
chapters.running_example: The verifier sees the patch and tests but lacks the policy history explaining why a removed check exists.
chapters.strongest_objection: Adequacy labels may become subjective gates that add delay without predicting contradictions.
chapters.failure_story: A concise summary preserves topic coverage but drops the one constraint that should block deployment.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Benchmarks showing no relation between declared adequacy, review allocation, and contradiction detection would require replacement.
chapters.handoff: The claim-review unit converts verification results into revisable beliefs and proof-carrying decisions.

chapters.reader_question: How should claims, defeaters, proof receipts, observations, disagreements, and revisions remain connected over time?
chapters.running_example: Bind the patch claim to sources, tests, verifier objections, effect observations, maximum inference, and downgrade triggers.
chapters.strongest_objection: A rich ledger can preserve immaculate metadata around a wrong conclusion and overwhelm meaningful review.
chapters.failure_story: A theorem receipt and two correlated reviews create confidence while the actual effect contradicts the recorded claim.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Simpler evidence records producing equal correction, calibration, and challenge performance would justify consolidation.
chapters.handoff: The work unit turns an accepted claim and plan into owned jobs, artifacts, acknowledgements, and replayable history.

chapters.reader_question: How should humans, agents, tools, and artifact stewards coordinate work without losing ownership, lineage, or accountability?
chapters.running_example: Issue typed jobs for drafting, checking, applying, observing, and recovering the repository change and join every artifact.
chapters.strongest_objection: A labor operating system may bureaucratize small tasks and shift responsibility into unread records.
chapters.failure_story: Each worker reports success, but the test belongs to another commit and no owner acknowledges the final effect.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Conventional issue, CI, and audit workflows matching continuity and recovery at lower burden would narrow the layer.
chapters.handoff: The runtime unit defines the narrow boundary where owned work becomes an external effect and ongoing operation.

chapters.reader_question: Which boundary should turn proposals into observed effects while preserving approval, incident, recovery, and graceful-degradation paths?
chapters.running_example: Apply the verified patch under a live grant, observe pre and post state, and retain exact rollback or compensation.
chapters.strongest_objection: Approval and adapter layers invite rubber-stamping while sophisticated tools find effects outside the declared boundary.
chapters.failure_story: A narrow file-edit approval is reused for deployment and tool success is reported as task success.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Simpler least-privilege wrappers matching effect observation, revocation, recovery, and incident handling would narrow the contract.
chapters.handoff: The substrate unit decides which cognitive architecture or specialist should serve each role behind these stable boundaries.

chapters.reader_question: How can routers choose among transformers, state-space models, recurrence, symbolic methods, tools, and future substrates?
chapters.running_example: Route patch generation, retrieval, verification, and rollback checks to different qualified substrates behind stable capability fields.
chapters.strongest_objection: Heterogeneous routing may add complexity and correlated failure without outperforming one well-tuned general model.
chapters.failure_story: A novel fast substrate wins a proxy benchmark, inherits qualification, and fails the rare dependency case it never saw.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Matched natural tasks showing no useful frontier gain after routing, migration, verification, and maintenance cost would favor monoculture.
chapters.handoff: The developmental-learning unit explains how those substrates acquire, consolidate, compose, and qualify new competence.

chapters.reader_question: How does the stack develop capability through training, interaction, intervention, memory, procedure, stabilization, and promotion?
chapters.running_example: Follow one repository-task candidate from frozen curriculum and full training state through learning, consolidation, regression, and qualification handoff.
chapters.strongest_objection: The developmental loop may be governance paperwork around standard training with no causal effect on learning quality.
chapters.failure_story: A checkpoint loads and scores well, but hidden state, data order, forgetting, and evaluator leakage make the claimed development irreproducible.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Strong standard training pipelines matching transfer, recovery, causal learning, and lifecycle cost would justify simplifying the loop.
chapters.handoff: The readiness unit decides when a candidate may advance while keeping benchmarks, safety cases, deception, and liveness visible.

chapters.reader_question: How should benchmarks, safety cases, adversarial evaluation, residuals, and bounded liveness determine readiness?
chapters.running_example: Qualify the changed repository verifier against positive controls, attacks, transfer, recovery, false blocks, and a finite quarantine route.
chapters.strongest_objection: Readiness gates can optimize benchmarks, hide residuals, and become safe only by preventing useful work.
chapters.failure_story: The candidate passes a contaminated suite and remains quarantined indefinitely whenever a natural task exposes uncertainty.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Simpler release practices matching defect escape, throughput, recovery, and governance cost would weaken the readiness system.
chapters.handoff: The economics unit prices useful cognition, infrastructure, verification, rollback, residuals, and governance on one ledger.

chapters.reader_question: When do routing and governance earn their compute, memory, storage, energy, latency, human, and recovery costs?
chapters.running_example: Compare repository-change routes on success, unsafe effects, false blocks, latency, reviewer effort, rollback, and lifecycle cost.
chapters.strongest_objection: Accounting can be gamed by excluding human burden, rare losses, transfer risk, and maintenance of governance itself.
chapters.failure_story: Token cost falls while review queues, stale caches, inexact rollback, and operator bypass move costs downstream.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Representative workloads where governance costs exceed avoided losses across risk tiers would require material simplification.
chapters.handoff: The integration unit joins recursive improvement, transitions, trust, development, recovery, and the Theseus prototype program.

chapters.reader_question: Do recursive improvement and all local controls compose into one observable, recoverable, and non-self-ratifying trace?
chapters.running_example: Replay the complete governed repository change and its attacks through the ASI-THESEUS-FLAGSHIP-01 design.
chapters.strongest_objection: A coherent reference trace may omit the open-world concurrency, institutions, adversaries, and recovery failures that break deployment.
chapters.failure_story: Locally valid components combine stale authority, a wrong receipt, and partial rollback into an unsafe release.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: End-to-end natural implementations with persistent composition failures would falsify specific interfaces and force architectural revision.
chapters.handoff: The final unit applies the same discipline to the book's sources, claims, derivatives, publication, and open challenges.

chapters.reader_question: Can the research program keep its ideas, sources, claims, proofs, corrections, products, and releases mutually accountable?
chapters.running_example: Treat this repository's prose-first convergence as a governed change that preserves support ceilings and leaves proof execution for its explicit gate.
chapters.strongest_objection: Elaborate self-governance may optimize records and publication surfaces instead of research quality or reader value.
chapters.failure_story: Local ledgers declare completion while ideas remain only in roadmaps and the public book exposes stale structure.
chapters.evidence_that_would_change_the_conclusio: Natural maintenance comparisons showing no improvement in correction, traceability, comprehension, or cost would require a smaller method.
chapters.handoff: The narrative route ends in the open challenge agenda: prove only the final bounded conclusions after every idea has an owner.

omission_policy: The other canonical chapters are not deleted, demoted, or treated as unimportant. Every narrative unit is a representative reading surface that routes to its compound and specialist owners in the complete 84-chapter architecture reference. Synthesis may shorten navigation but may not fork claim identity, erase uncertainty, or inherit evidence from an adjacent owner.
review_gate: Generate the derivative from the current canonical manifest rather than copying a parallel manuscript.
Verify that all twenty-two representative chapters exist, preserve canonical order, and carry current core-claim references.
Verify that every one of the 84 canonical chapters maps to exactly one narrative unit or remains explicitly discoverable as optional reference material.
Verify meaning preservation, handoffs, glossary terms, source and claim links, role ownership, browser navigation, and accessibility preparation.
Create an edition release record only for artifacts that were actually rendered and reviewed under the declared internal gates.
non_claims: Selection for the narrative route does not promote a chapter-core support state.
Omission as a representative unit does not reject, deprecate, merge, or remove a canonical chapter.
A generated candidate is not a reviewed reader release, publication artifact, empirical result, or independent approval.
Compound-unit synthesis does not transfer authority or evidence between canonical chapter owners.
The orientation fields are editorial navigation and add no evidence.
